t.2.2.1: The city of eleven gates belongs to the Unborn One, whose thought is not crooked; having attended to it, one does not grieve, and, being freed, he is set free. This, truly, is That.
t.2.2.2: He is the swan dwelling in the bright sky, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house; he dwells in men, he dwells in the excellent, he dwells in truth, he dwells in the heavens. Born of the waters, born of the cows, born of truth, born of the mountains, he is the truth, the great.
t.2.2.3: He leads the prāṇa upward and casts the apāna downward; all the gods worship that dwarf seated in the middle.
t.2.2.4: When this embodied one dwelling in the body slips away and is released from the body, what remains here? This, truly, is That.
t.2.2.5: No mortal whatsoever lives by prāṇa or by apāna; rather, they live by another, in which these two have their support.
t.2.2.6: Well then, I shall declare to you this secret and eternal Brahman, and also how the self fares after reaching death, O Gautama.
t.2.2.7: Some embodied beings enter a womb to take on a body; others go into a stationary thing, according to their deeds and according to their knowledge.
t.2.2.8: That Person who stays awake in those who sleep, fashioning desire after desire, that indeed is the bright, that is Brahman, that alone is called the immortal. In it all the worlds rest, and no one ever goes beyond it. This, truly, is That.
t.2.2.9: As the one fire, having entered the world, has become corresponding in form to every form, so the one inner Self of all beings takes the form of every form, and it is also outside.
t.2.2.10: As the one wind, having entered the world, has become corresponding in form to every form, so the one inner Self of all beings takes the form of every form, and yet remains outside as well.
t.2.2.11: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not tainted by the external faults of the eyes, so the one inner Self of all beings is not tainted by the sorrow of the world, being outside it.
t.2.2.12: The One, the controller, the inner Self of all beings, who makes his one form manifold: the wise who perceive him as abiding within the self, theirs is eternal happiness, not that of others.
t.2.2.13: The eternal among the non-eternal, the conscious among the conscious, the one among the many, who grants their desires: the wise who perceive him as abiding within the self, to them belongs eternal peace, not to others.
t.2.2.14: "This is that," so they think of the indescribable supreme bliss. How then may I know that? Does it shine of itself, or does it shine by reflection?
t.2.2.15: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine, how then this fire? Him alone, as he shines, does everything shine after; by his light all this shines forth.
